svg.title: Heating & practicals
svg.desc: Specific heat capacity: Energy to warm 1 kg by 1°C without a state change. Units: J/kg°C. ΔE = mcΔθ. Higher c → less warming for the same mass and input. Worked example: 0.50 kg water, c = 4,200 J/kg°C, warmed 20 → 40°C. Δθ = 20°C; ΔE = 0.50 × 4,200 × 20 = 42,000 J. Convert grams to kg first. Measure c: Balance → mass; thermometer → rise; joulemeter or Pt → energy. Insulate a block; improve heater/probe contact. Record initial temperature, heat, record rise. c = E/(mΔθ). Repeat; keep electrical parts dry; avoid hot surfaces. Explain error: Energy also heats equipment and surroundings. Using all input for the sample makes c too high. Insulation reduces losses. Good thermal contact reduces lag. Energy vs temperature-rise gradient = mc ideally. Insulators: Thicker material or lower conductivity → slower conduction under matching conditions. Trapped air reduces transfer; draught-proofing limits escaping warm air. Payback time = cost / yearly saving, assuming constant savings. Cooling investigation: Compare equal thicknesses; same containers, lids, water mass, starting temperature and room. Measure temperature at equal intervals; repeat and average. Smaller drop in same time → better insulation. For thickness: keep material fixed. Handle hot water safely.
